end.summary:
Practised ordering BCE and CE dates on a timeline, including 1 BCE, 1 CE, and 1947 CE.
Aarav placed CE dates to the right and BCE dates to the left of the middle.
Discussed archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources.
Aarav continued to treat one written source as fully reliable; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised timeline ordering with BCE years counting down toward 1 BCE, and Aarav correctly placed BCE on the left and CE on the right in the examples discussed. They also explored how inscriptions and oral traditions can provide information, but the mix-up that one written source gives the complete truth was not corrected by the end of the lesson (correctAfterLastSeen: 0). At home, compare one historical event using two sources and ask what each source tells us and what it may leave out.
